The represented family is I_rep = {Pois(λ): λ>0} ∪ {Bin(N,p): N∈N_0, p∈[0,1]} ∪ {NB(r,p): r∈N, p∈[0,1]} ∪ {Hyp(N_pop,K,M_draw): N_pop∈N, K∈{0,...,N_pop}, M_draw∈{0,...,N_pop}}; each P_S:N_0→[0,1] satisfies Σ_{n=0}^∞P_S(n)=1, with finite-support laws extended by P_S(n)=0 outside their support.

canonical_goal.target_object: A modular projection result in which an infinite count-basis state is mapped to an M-dimensional cyclic basis, total probability is preserved, residue probabilities P(Nˆ mod M=r) are exactly the discrete Fourier transform of the characteristic function φ(ω)=Σ_{n=0}^∞P(Nˆ=n)e^{iωn} sampled at ω=2πk/M, and the residue distribution converges exponentially to the uniform law P_U(r)=1/M for Negative Binomial, Binomial, and Poisson scale parameters.
feasibility_constraints: M is an integer with M≥2; H_M is a complex Hilbert space with orthonormal basis {|0⟩_M,...,|M-1⟩_M}; the modular projection Rˆ_M:H_∞→H_M is defined on the count basis by Rˆ_M|k⟩=|k mod M⟩_M for every k∈N_0.

For a normalized count state |ψ⟩=Σ_{k=0}^∞α_k|k⟩ with Σ_{k=0}^∞|α_k|^2=1, projected probabilities are P_M(r)=|β_r|^2=Σ_{j=0}^∞|α_{r+jM}|^2 for r∈{0,...,M-1}; choosing β_r=sqrt(P_M(r)) fixes a normalized representative |ψ_M⟩=Σ_{r=0}^{M-1}β_r|r⟩_M.
The characteristic function of the count distribution is φ(ω)=Σ_{n=0}^∞P(Nˆ=n)e^{iωn}; the residue distribution is evaluated on the finite cyclic group {0,...,M-1} by P_M(r)=Σ_{j=0}^∞P(Nˆ=r+jM).

The convergence subfamily is I_mod={NB(r,p):r∈N,p∈(0,1)}∪{Bin(n,p):n∈N,p∈(0,1)}∪{Pois(λ):λ>0}; for each nonzero Fourier frequency k∈{1,...,M-1}, the relevant characteristic-function magnitude is strictly less than 1 so that a bound |φ(2πk/M)|≤ρ^m can be chosen with 0<ρ<1 and m equal to r, n, or λ for NB, Binomial, or Poisson respectively.

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated goal is the joint proposition that there exists a count-basis Hilbert-space formalism (H_∞,{|n⟩},Nˆ,Hˆ_QHO,{|ψ_S⟩},{ΔV_S}) for Poisson, Binomial, Negative Binomial/Geometric, and Hypergeometric count laws with |α_n^(S)|^2=P_S(n); a modular projection Rˆ_M mapping count distributions to residue distributions P(Nˆ mod M=r)=M^{-1}Σ_{k=0}^{M-1}φ(2πk/M)e^{-2πikr/M}, where φ(ω)=Σ_{n=0}^∞P(Nˆ=n)e^{iωn}, that converge to 1/M for Negative Binomial, Binomial, and Poisson families; and a named-family quantum probability-engineering claim in which perturbations of Hˆ_QHO realise or encode the target probability law, with an explicit Poisson Hamiltonian and algebraic perturbation structures for Binomial, Negative Binomial/Geometric, and Hypergeometric systems.

operational_goal.formalisation: The operational goal is the conjunction of three formal end-states: (1) construct count-basis states |ψ_S⟩=Σ_nα_n^(S)|n⟩ with |α_n^(S)|^2=P_S(n) for Poisson, Binomial, Negative Binomial/Geometric, and Hypergeometric laws, together with operator identities for moments and information quantities; (2) define Rˆ_M|k⟩=|k mod M⟩_M, prove Σ_r|β_r|^2=1, express P(Nˆ mod M=r) as a finite Fourier sum of φ(2πk/M), and bound nonzero Fourier modes by O(ρ^m); and (3) formulate quantum stochastic engineering for the same named laws, using the explicit Poisson perturbation ΔV_Pois=ℏω(-αaˆ†-α*aˆ+|α|^2) and the paper's finite-rank, geometric-plus-correlation, and projection-constraint perturbation structures for the other named families. Section V's dynamical, tensor-product, master-equation, and spectral formulas are treated as an extension of the first end-state rather than as a separate coordinate goal.

inference_basis: The abstract and introduction foreground three central end-states: a Hilbert-space/operator framework for stochastic systems, modular projection/TURNG uniformity, and quantum probability engineering through perturbations of the quantum harmonic oscillator.

Sections II-IV contain the strongest formal artefacts: Hamiltonians and count-basis amplitudes in Section II, modular projection and Fourier convergence in Section III, and perturbation/engineering statements in Section IV.

Section V supplies formal equations for dynamics, tensor-product correlations, noisy evolution, and spectral modes, but these equations extend the Hilbert-space formalism rather than introducing a separate success criterion comparable to the Section II-IV goals.

The broad Section IV theorem for arbitrary P(n) is stronger than the distribution-specific constructions given for Poisson, Binomial, Negative Binomial/Geometric, and Hypergeometric laws, so the extraction records named families as the claimed operational subfamily and arbitrary normalized P:N_0→[0,1] as a hinted superfamily.

The evaluation artefacts are theorem statements, algebraic identities, and convergence tables rather than optimisation metrics; therefore the goals are target propositions or constrained satisfiability statements rather than objective functionals.

Interpretive claims that stochastic systems are fundamentally quantum-mechanical or bridge multiple fields are broader than the operational artefacts and are therefore treated as framing rather than standalone canonical goals.
implicit_goal.formalisation: The best-fit implicit extraction is a joint conjunction of three coordinate goals: represent Poisson, Binomial, Negative Binomial/Geometric, and Hypergeometric count laws as normalized count-basis states satisfying |α_n|^2=P(n) and operator identities for moments and information quantities; prove modular projection identities and exponential convergence to the uniform residue law for Negative Binomial, Binomial, and Poisson families; and formulate named-family quantum stochastic engineering for those distributions, with the arbitrary normalized discrete distribution family H_eng^+={P:N_0→[0,1]:Σ_nP(n)=1} recorded as a broader stated/hinted superfamily rather than as the operationally established core. This implicit goal is preferred over a four-goal extraction because the dynamical material i d|ψ(t)⟩/dt=Hˆ_S|ψ(t)⟩, tensor products, master equations, and spectral decompositions extend the first Hilbert-space goal without supplying an independent paper-level success predicate.

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The stated and operational channels agree on three central mathematical end-states: count-basis Hilbert-space representation, modular projection with Fourier-based convergence to uniformity, and named-family quantum probability engineering. The stated channel additionally contains broader interpretive and application framing, including that stochastic systems are fundamentally quantum-mechanical, that the work bridges several fields, and that dynamical/correlated systems can be developed as an extension.
